utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Witness. We are continuing with cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everybody taking part in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Novak Lukic. I'm the attorney and Defence counsel for Mr. Miroslav Tadic, and I'll be asking you a few questions on his behalf. I should like to ask you, as we did yesterday with respect to clarity and time economy, to give us brief answers: "yes," "no," or "I don't know." Let us go back to the events you were describing when you were arrested and the circumstances of your arrest. On Easter, the 19th, I think you were arrested and taken to the SUP premises, and from there you were transferred to the TO warehouse; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were arrested on the 18th and transferred to the TO warehouse on the 19th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was arrested on the 18th, and on the 19th, or the 20th, in the morning -- but I think it was the 19th, yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before noon?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you encountered 20 to 30 people who were there already?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All the people went there together with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the warehouse was actually empty before you all went into it, before you were transferred from the SUP premises to the TO warehouse; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, Dragan Lukac was transferred together with you, was he not?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that - I think that he was -- had still not been brought in - whether he was transferred from the SUP to the TO or whether he was brought in later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but he was at the TO until you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The brothers Bicic, Hasan and Muhamed, were they transferred to the TO building together with you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were brought in later, but then they stayed with us all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. Tihic? Was he in the TO building too with you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came later. He was brought in later, like the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he wasn't there on that weekend, was he, none of those people?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Izet Izetbegovic, how about him? Was he in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he wasn't brought together with us from the SUP, but he was brought in later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, all these people except Izetbegovic were transferred to Brcko the following week for Easter, the 26th, as far as I know, unless I'm wrong on the dates.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Salkic, did you see Mr. Miroslav Tadic while were you in the TO warehouse?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should like to move on to another area now. In your examination-in-chief, you said that you would like to go back to the topic that I'm going to discuss, but the Prosecutor didn't ask you any questions on that topic further. What I'm talking about is your description of the events between the 16th and 17th and your meeting with Mr. Namik Suljic. You said that he called the policeman standing on the bridge, on page 322 actually, and later on it turned out that Namik was right because all those people were also incarcerated, and I'm quoting your words, what you said. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many policemen there actually were at the checkpoint on the bridge across the Sava River?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that four people were detained, three, but actually I think there were four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And they were all taken to the TO building or the SUP?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were already in the SUP building and they were taken to the TO with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they wearing police uniforms?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Talking about uniforms, you mentioned people who were detained in Brcko - or Batkovici, I'm sorry. I meant Batkovici - and you said that there were several officers of the former JNA. You assumed they were officers, otherwise they were wearing civilian clothing. Now, do you recall that in Batkovic, together with you, Lucic, Ivo and Sacic, Boris were incarcerated with you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that they were soldiers of the Croatian army from Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had heard something about that along those lines, but I couldn't be sure because they were in civilian clothing and I didn't talk to them much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that some friends talked about the formation of units set up by citizens themselves for the organisation of the town, that you didn't actually join because you didn't have time for things like that. I'm interested in knowing the following: Can you remember, when they told you about this newly established TO, who told you about that?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Friends and acquaintances from town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody invite you to go there?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I went at my own initiative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief on the 1st of November, 2001, you said that when you came to where the people were being registered, that that was the real thing, the proper thing, that "we were together again." You said something like that?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw the members of all three ethnic groups and you were happy to see them there. That was something that you were happy to see; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone force you to sign up to this newly established TO?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you went inside, that you waited for about half an hour, if I remember correctly, and that then you signed a joining-up document. I remember you saying that. Do you happen to remember what it said on this membership formula?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. It was a list and there was a form to fill in that had come from the ministry, that it was saying that it was a legal institution of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that anybody could take part and become a member who were in favour of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And I was in favour of it, so I subscribed to the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but nobody forced you to place your signature there?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did it of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, pausing, pausing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about the others who were there with you? Were they forced to sign the form to enlist?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think so. There was nobody to force them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you -- would there have been any kind of sanctions for punishment if you did not join up?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was my moral duty towards my country, as an able-bodied man, to become a member of that organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody force you to become a member of the Fazan hunting society?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that after you did your military service, you were assigned to the Territorial Defence of the old SFRY, within the frameworks of the armed forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we take it, then, that after doing your military service, you were called up to report to the Secretariat for National Defence to be given your wartime assignment as a member of the reserve formation of the armed forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We even had some training and some practice, which is quite normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you not gone to the Secretariat for National Defence to respond to the call-up, would they have taken any sanctions against you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the system that existed then, I would have been criminally prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you not gone to the military exercises and training, would you have been criminally prosecuted as well?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, all the call-ups for military training, it said on the invitation you received, that failure to respond to the call-up would imply sanctions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have just a few more questions for you. Mr. Salkic, did you, since you were freed and at liberty and since the war ended, did you go to Samac at all?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequently, can you tell us, and when did you start going back to Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you the exact date. But when I returned from Germany, that was July or August 1998, so from that time onwards, whenever I was able to, I went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often? Once a month perhaps or ...

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes even three times a day. Sometimes I wouldn't go for a month, depending on the circumstances and whether I had any need to go into town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do any work, professionally speaking, relating to your trade? Did you have any business dealings in Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of late, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have one more question for you. You described in detail in this courtroom the beatings that took place, the beatings by people who beat others from outside Samac, from Serbia, and also people from that area. Now, during your stay in Samac, did you see any of the people who beat you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you. [In English] Your Honour, I've finished cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The last counsel, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Salkic.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am Borislav Pisarevic, Defence counsel for Mr. Simo Zaric. Before we begin with the cross-examination, I should like to say the following, and that is that Mr. Zaric, Mr. Simo Zaric, and I, acting as his Defence counsel, would like to express our profound condolences for all your sufferings and hardships during this unfortunate war. As you said, you and your family have lived in the town and municipality of Samac for many years. May we take it that in addition to the Muslims, Serbs, and Croats, Bosanski Samac was inhabited by quite a number of Yugoslavs, people who declared themselves as Yugoslavs, and Montenegrins, Albanians, and other nations and nationalities?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we also take it that the Muslim ethnic group in the town of Bosanski Samac numbered 25 per cent, approximately?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be sure of the percentage, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. May we also agree that in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, taken as a broader area, the Muslims numbered approximately 7 per cent?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Seven point something per cent. So my answer is yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you knew Simo Zaric and that you have known him for 25 to 30 years.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree, then, that Simo Zaric, in the town of Samac and the municipality itself, was a respected citizen?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can, fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we also agree that Mr. Simo Zaric never demonstrated any lack of tolerance?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lack of tolerance towards other people, regardless of their national and ethnic affiliation?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up until one point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he demonstrate tolerance to religious affiliation of citizens?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say, his wife is a Muslim herself, so he did not --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you didn't understand me, Mr. Salkic. My question was as follows: Was Mr. Zaric tolerant towards other religious affiliation?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he show tolerance towards different political affiliation of citizens?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say of late, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Zaric have a positive attitude towards all the citizens, regardless of their social status?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you the following: Do you happen to know that the wife of Mr. Simo Zaric is Muslim?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up to a certain point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me when I say that Simo Zaric was a true supporter of the idea of Yugoslavhood and Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were a member of the Fazan hunting society of Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm and do we agree that Simo Zaric was also a member of the Fazan hunting society of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We even went hunting together sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just wait for my answers [as interpreted], please.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your hunting society numbered about 15 members.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This number changed. Some people would turn up, others wouldn't, but more or less there were between 10 and 15 of us in our group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that your hunting group was composed of different ethnic groups, nationalities?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May we also take it that there were members of different religions in your hunting society too?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that among the members of your hunting group there were members with different political views and affiliations?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you also agree that in your hunting group there were workers, tradesmen, entrepreneurs, members of the police force, respected citizens, and intellectuals alike?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me when I say that according to the rules and regulations governing hunting societies, you could only hunt in the hunting season, when hunting was permitted within the frameworks of a hunting group?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me too that the hunting season, open season, ended in November?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you a yes or no answer there. It depended. It depended on the weather conditions. Sometimes we could go up to the new year. Sometimes the end of the season would be in December, mid-December. But more or less up to new year, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When was the hunting season declared open in the spring?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it opens on the 1st of June. Open season the 1st of June. The official opening of the season begins sometime around the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we also take it that in this period of time, when it was closed season, your hunting group met less frequently, very rarely or hardly at all?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did meet nevertheless. We would meet on weekdays, but we didn't go hunting, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as hunting was concerned, you met rarely?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but we used to socialise. So it was that group that would meet from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. As far as I'm aware - and you'll correct me if I'm wrong - all the members of the hunting organisation had to have hunting weapons to go hunting with?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have to. They could be members of the hunting society and not possess a rifle, but those were rare cases in our parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the majority.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That would be right, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, I think, that shotguns -- shotguns were used for pheasants, rabbits, and smaller game, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you'll also agree with me when I say that carbines were used for larger game?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such as deer, boars, and so on?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we agree that many hunters in Samac, and the members of your group too, hunting group, owned carbines?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm the following fact, that the carbine was a weapon which is not an automatic weapon? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you answer this: How many bullets are there in a carbine ammunition box?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones we had, the ones we used when we hunted together, there were a maximum of five or six and then the additional bullets in the barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you give us the calibre of that ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depending on the different calibres, we had different calibre carbines. 857, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume that using that kind of ammunition, you can also kill a bear, deer, and so forth, but that you could also kill a human being using the same ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Big-game hunting is done at a distance of several hundred metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depending on the target, whether you have an optic sight, a sniper or not. And you had to do it from a special vantage point, looking down on to your target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You needn't go into the details. Can you confirm that with a carbine -- or rather, on a carbine itself, you usually have an optic sight for precision targeting, in view of the distance at which you are shooting?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for those of us who had money to purchase the optic sight or who needed to use it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May we also agree that a carbine with optic sight is in fact a weapon known under the common term of "sniper"?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's what we called it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salkic, in view of the fact that you spent your whole life living in Bosanski Samac, I'm going to ask you several questions concerning some events that took place in the municipality of Samac and the town of Samac itself. I'm sure you know that at the end of 1991 and in the course of 1992, in Samac municipality, various sabotage activities took place, there were various explosions and things of that kind?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure you will recall the event that took place on the 27th of January, 1992, when the Serbian Orthodox church was demolished in Bosanski Samac on their saint day, St. Sava's Day?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, believe me when I say that I don't actually remember that. I'm not saying that it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You say you don't remember. You are aware of an event when two young Muslim men were killed and a girl of Serbian nationality was seriously wounded on the 14th of February, 1992, in the Valentino Cafe?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that on that occasion, the populace of the town of Samac was very disturbed, upset, especially the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I think people of every nationality were upset.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but mostly Muslims. Are you aware that this event was used to blame the Serbs, the JNA, and accuse them of being involved in this event?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me just a brief comment, my own view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course there were rumours, but the truth was known. Unfortunately, it was tragic for those people in that cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that because of the mounting tension and the fact that the citizens of Samac were disturbed, a rally was held in the cinema in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that rally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you must be aware of the fact that the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action, and its military wing, on the 21st of March, 1992, set up barricades at the entrance to Bosanski Samac from the villages of Tisina and another village?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume you are also aware of the leaflet that was distributed on the 1st of April, 1992, around Samac about traitors, drawn up by the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I only heard about it. But who wrote it and who distributed it, I really don't know. I have heard of this leaflet, but I cannot say either yes or no, because I myself never saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn in some other way who the people were mentioned in that leaflet?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that that leaflet contained the names of members of the 4th Detachment of the JNA who were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me another comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Either you know or you don't.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if you will allow me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I say "yes and no" and then just give a little comment? There were rumours going around town, but I myself never saw the leaflet. I know more or less who the people were mentioned in the rumours. I myself never saw the leaflet. I don't know who issued it. But people talked about it in town. So I can say both yes and no, but I cannot be certain, because I myself never saw it, so I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people say that the people were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel and the witness, please pause. You are not conversing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I believe you are aware of the wounding of Osman Mesic and Danilo and others near the Mol Cafe [phoen] in Bosanski Samac. Can we agree that all these events contributed to a high degree of insecurity among the citizens of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, you said that you were a member of the SDA and that you left the party six months before the outbreak of hostilities in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether it was six or five, it's not really important. Mr. Salkic, in the period from the 3rd of March to the 7th of March, 1992, were you a member of the patrol organised by the SDA in the town of Samac without receiving any remuneration for your participation like the other participants?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never in an SDA patrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that you were at the barricade on the 21st of March, 1992? And I'm referring to the barricade near the veterinary station.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me that you were called up by Alija Fitozovic, the commander of the party armed formation for the town of Samac, and told to participate in manning this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I came on my own initiative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn, Mr. Salkic, that barricades were being set up at the entrance to the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a phone call from someone, and he explained to me that the war had already broken out - not war as such, but there were problems - and I got into my car and went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the checkpoints were manned exclusively by members of the Party of Democratic Action, members who were Muslims, members of the armed party unit, and reserve policemen of the public security station in Bosanski Samac who were of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree about some of these details, but not overall. So if you will allow me to comment, nobody had a label stuck to their foreheads saying whether they were party members or this or that. Yes, you're right that most of them were Muslims. A few were Croats, and there were policemen, but who the formations belonged to, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we agree that the people manning the checkpoints were armed with military weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, were you at the barricades with the weapon you had bought illegally, your Kalashnikov? Was that the Kalashnikov you bought for a thousand German marks?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, because the question was double-barrelled, I don't know if the witness is saying, "Yes, that's the Kalashnikov I bought for a thousand German marks" or whether he's agreeing -- that the Kalashnikov he bought cost a thousand German or whether he was at the barricades. I think he might be answering yes to both, but the question should be framed differently so that we're clear about that. I would like to know, and it's a little bit unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure the witness has understood what you are saying and he can explain his answer. And, Counsel, do make sure that your questions are not loaded. One aspect at a time, please. So, Mr. Salkic, please explain your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was there with that Kalashnikov which I had bought and paid for with my own money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were buying this Kalashnikov, did you also buy ammunition for it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time, but I did later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you bought your Kalashnikov, did you also buy ammunition for it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm the fact that you got ammunition for that Kalashnikov - 4 rounds, 40 armour-piercing weapons, 45 piercing bullets, and 40 incendiary bullets - from the party armed formation, commanded by Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never received ammunition from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm to me, or deny, the fact that from Alija Fitozovic, the commander of the party armed unit and later on the Chief of Staff of the Territorial Defence, that he gave you a uniform of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina with lilies and that it was a green uniform.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from Alija, but from the people in Cafe Buco, from some people I knew. I never, never received a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, you received a patch?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had a patch. I never received either a uniform or a patch from Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you are talking about the patch, are you referring to the lilies I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the fleurs-de-lis were the official emblem of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it is official, I couldn't say. I simply got them from a friend and they were the symbol of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, if I could ask Mr. Salkic. You, in response to a question, said that you did not get a uniform from Alija. Your answer is, "Not from Alija, but from the people in Cafe Buco." I'm just wondering, Mr. Salkic, what did you get from the people in the cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I probably wasn't clear. Only the patch. I didn't have a uniform because I had my hunting uniform and I didn't need any other uniform, nor was I getting ready for war so that I would require a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, this patch that you received, did you wear it openly around the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion, I stuck it onto my hunting uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So the patch you received, you wore on your hunting uniform?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, are you aware of the fact that the presidency of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia on the 13th of December, 1991, when -- while Bosnia and Herzegovina was still part of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, established a general mobilisation of military-able persons?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, you did not respond to the call-up of the JNA? You did not report to the 4th Detachment of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't receive the call-up, but even if I had, I certainly would not have responded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You will agree with me that as a citizen and a military-able person, it was your duty to respond?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. And if you will allow me a short comment, I'll explain why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no need. There is no need. Can we agree that you did not respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm not clear with the time perspective with regard to the answer of Mr. Salkic, because at first he said he didn't receive the call-up, but even if he had, he would not have joined, and then he was explaining it was not necessary. I want to know what he means. Was it at that time? Because he didn't receive the call-up, so he couldn't have said at that time that it was not necessary to join. And then you can't put it to him that it was wrong not to join, if his answer is that he didn't receive the call-up. So I would like Mr. Salkic to explain what he means. Did he receive the call-up or he didn't. If he did, did he find it necessary to join or to answer the call or not to? Can we have an explanation, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I will be very brief. There was already a war in Slovenia and Croatia. I knew that draft notes were being sent out. I was not at home very often. And I told my wife, "You must not receive the draft note. I do not want to join the Yugoslav People's Army to go to neighbouring Croatia and kill innocent people." That's my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that apart from the reasons you have mentioned just now, you did not respond to the call-up because you are a Muslim and Alija Izetbegovic, the president of the SDA, on the 7th of October, 1991, publicly called on all Muslims not to respond to call-ups to do their regular military service or to the draft notes?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I will not agree. I would like to comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no need to comment.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree. I wouldn't agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of this appeal made by President Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe yes, maybe no. Basically I don't remember it, so -- I already had my view of things, so I did not need any suggestions from outside. I don't know about it. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, perhaps I'm missing something here, but I don't know what appeal by President Alija Izetbegovic Mr. Pisarevic refers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Where? MR. DI FAZIO: Line 19, there is a question: "Do you know of this appeal?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. You don't understand the appeal, what he means? MR. DI FAZIO: No. If I'm missing something, then I don't need to pursue it, but I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The counsel can explain. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm concerned that the Chamber might have my difficulty as well, so I just wonder if that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes, because I think just a little earlier at 14102149, he said, "The president of the SDA on the 7th of October, 1991, publicly called on all Muslims not to respond to the call-up to do their military service." MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Because that question is double-barrelled, because if you look at it, "You did not respond," and then, "Did he say this?" So I mean, it's very difficult for him to answer this question. So one question at a time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to make a correction, if I may, Your Honour, just to correct something. He was then the legally elected president of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not the party president of the SDA. So that he probably did issue a public appeal to the population, but I do not feel that he was the president of the SDA but he was the president of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the implication there is that he made that appeal in his capacity as president of B and H, not president of the party? Is that so, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. His Honour said the president of the SDA. I didn't want this to be misunderstood. He was then the legally elected president of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it was probably in this capacity that he made this proclamation to the people, but I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we shall clarify the situation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that Alija Izetbegovic was the president of the Party of Democratic Action in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, you said he was the president. Can we agree that he was not the president of Bosnia and Herzegovina but that Mr. Alija Izetbegovic was the president of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So I probably didn't express myself properly, but the president, yes. There was a presidency, then, at the time probably. I'm not very familiar with this, but yes, in essence, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that even at the cost of having criminal proceedings instituted against you for the criminal act of failure to respond to a call-up, you decided not to respond to the call-up?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive the draft note. It was never handed to me. I explained how I avoided having it handed to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your statement, when Tihic, Pasaga, informed you of events in the town, you took your Kalashnikov and some ammunition, put on your hunting uniform, and set out towards the centre of town. Is that correct? On your hunting equipment that evening, were you wearing the patch of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I don't want to be pedantic, and again it's the same problem. What's the answer "no" to: whether he was wearing the patch or whether he went to the town with his Kalashnikov and some ammunition? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Again, it was a loaded question, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: It's just two questions. Do one at a time, and then there's no ambiguity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic -- MR. DI FAZIO: And one other matter is the - and Mr. Weiner points out to me - the occasion is not identified. I think it's the barricades episode that Mr. Pisarevic is referring to, but again, that should be -- it should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let counsel break down the questions, and also identify the event, possibly the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, on the 17th of April, 1992, at around 2.00, you were informed [redacted] of some events in the town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took your Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took some ammunition for it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did. Why would I carry an empty gun?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are simply clarifying. You put on your hunting uniform?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You set out toward the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you carry binoculars with you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take your Motorola?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Kalashnikov that you did take with you, was it the same Kalashnikov that you had purchased and that you were at the barricades carrying on the 22nd of March in Bosanski Samac by the vet clinic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the ammunition that you took? Was it the ammunition that you had received from the party SDA armed formation in Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I state again that I did not receive any ammunition from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where and when -- where did you procure that ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was very easy to do that before the war. I bought it on the black market. They had plenty of it, and I paid one Deutschmark per bullet. That was the going price.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that on the occasion you met Suljic, Namik, the commander of the reserve police force of the public security station of Samac, who was on duty that particular night.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that from your house, you [redacted] [redacted] left your house [redacted] at about 2.15?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we also take it that you met Namik Suljic at about 2.30?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean to say that you and [redacted] and Namik Suljic were in front of the hotel in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We met up there. We found ourselves there later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you state whether you moved to the park in Bosanski Samac after that, which is opposite the hotel, on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the park, but in front of the SDK, or social accounting services building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your testimony before this Tribunal, you stated, on page 3220, line 25 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. We have a comment regarding the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This witness said that they went to the park place, something, and we don't see this in the transcript, so maybe it would be good to clarify this at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the counsel can ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After meeting up in front of the hotel, did you go to the park compound?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to describe that. You have the hotel on one side and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate that to us on the map. Could you draw it for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is to say, could the witness be shown the map of Samac, which is Exhibit P9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But at the same time, you want him to make out a sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate with the pointer the hotel building in Bosanski Samac. Could you point it out to us.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the new hotel, that's the old hotel, that's the SDK building, and the park. That is where we met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you met in the park area?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't have a car go into the park, so we stopped there and we were on the corner by this kiosk, but it already belonged to the park section.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, may we note that the witness indicated the part of the park in which the witness Salkic stood [redacted] Namik Suljic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And many others. And many others already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... MR. DI FAZIO: I was just about to say that it should be identified where the marking -- a number or something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps a circle with an "X" inside. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, you said a moment ago that many other people were there too. These other people, the many other people that you mentioned, were they in the park?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some came through the park, some came along the road, because you could hear the shooting round about the SUP building already, and people had taken to their feet. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you proceed, can we have a number, please, for the sketch by Mr. Salkic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D10/4 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how many people were in the park at that moment?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three, four, five maybe, depending on who was on the move. Some came via the road, others came from another direction, other people were sitting in the cafe at Ena's, because it worked around the clock. So in the 10 or 15 minutes that I was there, there might have been 10 to 12 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you confirm the following fact: that these people came with weapons, carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them, at least, but probably there were some who did have weapons. Namik was a policeman, so he was armed. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] And then people came in. Now, whether they did or didn't, I don't know. It was already dark. But I was armed. I can claim that for myself, but I can't say about the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you're saying that some people were armed and others were not. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was me and Namik. They were the ones that I said were armed. Some other people were not armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who came to the park in Bosanski Samac, were they -- were some of them carrying army weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps. I can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say that you saw people coming?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've just told you, there were four to five people to begin with, later on, ten people before I had left and went on further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we also agree that you stayed in that park until 5.00 a.m., 5.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony before this Court, you said, on page 3220, line 25, the following: "We then decided to move off towards the river and the bridge." On page 3221, line 10, you say that it was the bridge on the river Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher's assistance? Could he show the witness his statement, the statement he made on the 7th to the 9th of February, 1992, the Serbo-Croatian version or the B/C/S version, which has the portions marked and so it is marked also in the English version. It is page 00637751, line 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness read it out, please. But if you find it difficult to read it out, I shall be happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I assume there is an error in the transcript here. It says, "The statement he made on the 7th to the 9th of February, 1992." I'm presuming this is the 1995 statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1995, yes, Your Honour. Thank you. 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness should read the passage slowly so that the interpreters can interpret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the 6th line: [redacted]..."

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read that? "I went [redacted] to a command post set up in a private house nearby. This was now about 5.00 a.m. We tried to contact some of our people we could rely upon and who had weapons. I went with Nedim Alajbegovic to the bridge over the Bosna River, since we had a major headquarters across the river in Prud."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that those two statements of yours are in opposition to each other, contradictory, whereas they are about the same event that took place?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I can't explain that without making a comment. May I be allowed to comment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, which command post did you [redacted] go to which was set up in a private house nearby? That means nearby the hotel and park.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in fact a group of people who -- there was probably a mistake in the translation. They were self-organised citizens. They were a larger group of people, and we had decided that should an attack or aggression of this kind take place on our town, that we were to meet up there, and then to see what we were going to do next. And with respect to the village of Prud --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said self-organised group of citizens. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That self-organised group of citizens, was it armed with military automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander or commanding officer of that self-organised group of citizens, was he Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was a group of narrow circle of my friends, and if you want, I can give you their names. [redacted]-- Dasa Gibic, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us the names for the record?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was Gibic, Osman, nicknamed Semso. There were about 10 of us, 10 to 15 of us who were a group of friends that met up quite often. We socialised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to these people, were the Bicic brothers there too?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were probably somewhere else, because they had a lot of work at that time, so they weren't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I take it they were not there, then? Is the answer no?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your self-organised group of citizens, did it have a command of any kind?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me who determined this command post, as you refer to it?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was probably an error in the translation. It was a collection point. This "command post" was probably a mistake in the translation, but it was the point that we had agreed to meet and that was around Buco's Cafe where we would always stop by. That's where we would go when we were socialising.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This collection point or rallying point or whatever you like to call it, can you state and confirm - or meeting point - that in the call-up and the draft note that was sent out by the Secretariat for National Defence, and in the military booklet, army booklet, when you were mobilised, that the meeting point was designated in the draft note and the booklet?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting to the line of cross-examination or to the subject matter, but I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: What draft note sent out by the secretariat? And are they saying that the meeting point, whatever this draft note was, was Buco's Cafe? Is that the idea?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we do need clarification. MR. DI FAZIO: I just don't understand the question. I don't object to the topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Secretariat for National Defence, which one? The government one? If we can have clarification, if you can break up the questions again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall try to clear this point up with the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you used the term "meeting point"?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that self-organised group of citizens, or units --

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not unit, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Group, then -- had determined a meeting point, and the meeting point was in Buco's Cafe, is that right -- or rather, the cafe belonging to Mesic, Osman, nicknamed Buco or Semso; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had done your military service in the Yugoslav People's Army and when you received your wartime assignment, in your military booklet, in case of mobilisation, the members of the reserve formation of the Yugoslav People's Army, as such, you had a certain meeting point to which you were to report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm waiting for you to ask the question. Very well, my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You further state that you tried to establish contact with people whom you could trust and who were armed?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those people the people who belonged to your self-organised group of citizens?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Some -- well, when we saw what was happening, we were very glad to take anybody in who was willing to join us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether at that meeting point -- how many people responded and came to the meeting point?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you know the town, and as you know that it is in the centre of town, surrounded by buildings, there were loads of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many? Ten? A hundred?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe 50, 100. They would all flow down from the street because it was a junction of four or six streets, so people were flowing into the centre from the side streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Mr. Salkic, that all this was happening during the night, between the -- on the 17th of April, 1992, in the early hours of the morning, in fact?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just don't agree with the date. It was the night between the 16th and the 17th. So it wasn't the night of the 17th. It was the early morning of the 17th, the early hours of the morning of the 17th of April. Perhaps we didn't agree on that point, or I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said on the 17th, in the early morning hours, and I used the term "night" to mean darkness; it was still dark then.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I understand. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this would be an opportune moment to take a break, Your Honours, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How many more minutes? Because you indicated yesterday that an hour, and you had one hour and 15 minutes. How many more minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 30, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because we are worried about completing Mr. Tihic this week. So yes, I will allow you not one minute more. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll do our best and get through it within that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll have our break --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and resume the proceedings at 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Salkic, you said that around 5.00, you and Alijbegovic, Nedim went to the bridge over the river Bosna "since we had a major HQ over the river in Prud." Can we agree that that "major HQ," as it says in the statement, was the command or headquarters of the Croatian army and Croatian Defence Council in the Croatian village of Prud?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. But let me clarify one point, and then I could give you an affirmative answer after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the Croatian component of the Croatian army, the army from Croatia; it was, as I heard it, a Crisis Staff, and probably it was composed of Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived at the bridge, on the embankment you came across a patrol of the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the members of the 4th Detachment patrol wearing?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing the SMB olive-green/grey uniforms of the Yugoslav army, the Yugoslav People's Army of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they prevent you from crossing the bridge?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, no, but when I started to move towards -- move on the bridge, then they shot at me, those same people from the 4th Detachment. So let me clarify this question in order to be able to give you a yes or no answer. They did not prevent me going on the bridge, but afterwards they shot at me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the question that I was going to ask you.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I apologise, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the members of this patrol, including Trivo and two other members, did they shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty, because from that direction and from the left-hand side, the shots were coming at me while I was on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please ask the witness and counsel to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we then take it that you're not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, can you speak into the microphone, please. The interpreters are having difficulties. And the witness can have his chair pushed toward the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an agreement -- about an agreement reached in the local community of Samac, according to which the members of the 4th Detachment were to patrol the embankment around the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You make mention of some bunkers on the left-hand side of the bridge and some snipers' nests. Can we take it that that is one and the same thing?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us more or less how far those snipers' nests were away from the bridge over the Bosna River?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they 500 metres away? Did the witness say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The distance, it was 300 to 350 metres away at the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see the snipers' nests yourself, or did you notice them when the firing started from them?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew about them from before, because those snipers' nests were set up five or six days beforehand, and I learnt about them five to six days before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The snipers' nests, were they on the embankment, or in the fields?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the fields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you crossed into Prud, where did you go to? Did you -- yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come across Alija Fitozovic there, the Chief of Staff of the TO and commander of the party unit?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, I'm just a bit concerned about the question and the answer there and what precisely the witness is agreeing to. There has been evidence that Alija Fitozovic was Chief of Staff of the TO, and I think this witness has said that he held some command position in the TO, but Mr. Pisarevic went on to put a second limb to the question, that he was commander of the party unit, and I don't think this witness, from what I recall from his evidence -- from what I recall of his evidence, has said anything about party units. And I don't know which party; I assume the SDA. And so it's that second aspect of the question that troubles me, and I don't know what the witness is agreeing to, both the things, that he was Chief of Staff of the TO and commander of the party unit, or only one or whatever. And it's important to know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Or that he came across Fitozovic, yes. There are three parts. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, or that he came across. It's not the coming across that concerned me. It's what he is agreeing to about Alija Fitozovic. Is he agreeing that he was Chief of Staff and commander of the party unit? That, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness has heard and the witness can explain his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I answered in the affirmative to the part of the question of whether I had seen Mr. Alija Fitozovic there. As to the positions he held, I can't confirm that. That is to say, I can confirm that he was in the command, whether he was the Chief of Staff or whatever in the legal institution and officially in the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in Prud, you received a Motorola; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you saw a motorised column of military vehicles in Prud on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With Alija Fitozovic, the Chief of Staff of the TO of Samac, did you, together with him, try to return to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I succeeded in crossing, whereas Mr. Fitozovic, from the shooting at the bridge, did not succeed. I don't know whether he did later on or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we take it, then, that you returned to Bosanski Samac at about 8.00 on the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was quite a bit earlier than that, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in Prud, did you hear an announcement over the radio, Radio Samac, calling upon the citizens to surrender their weapons, which -- if they possessed any illegal weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I heard that when I had returned to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, with the Motorola you had, call units of the Croatian army from the Republic of Croatia and the Croatian Defence Council from Prud to come to assist the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again for me to say yes or no, I have to explain, I have to comment. I have to comment the titles and names of those formations, if I may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me if you called any of them or not.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the Croatian army, nor was it the HVO. It was still the legal -- the legal unit, either of the TO or the local community which existed in that village, the village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we agree, then, that you used your Motorola to call members -- to call up members of the units of the Prud local community to come to the assistance of people in the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I explained the situation to them. I tried to contact -- come into contact with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Do you know that Alija Fitozovic, the Chief of Staff of the TO, returned to Samac, Bosanski Samac, across the bridge on the river Bosna, at about 10.00 on the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was to learn about that only when I was exchanged, later on, when I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that you were not aware of the fact that Alija Fitozovic, as Chief of Staff of the TO, took over the command of members of the unit which was located in the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you're saying is that you don't know that the -- that means that you don't know that the demarcation line in the town of Bosanski Samac existed?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's right, because I still moved around town, and I know where the different units were, the formations of the 4th Detachment and the special forces that we call them, the Chetniks, who were in collaboration with the 4th Detachment and the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means, if I understood you correctly, that in that part of town, freely and unimpeded, the members of the Territorial Defence could move around, and the self-organised citizens of Samac municipality. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether they were allowed to move around freely or not, I don't know, but they could move around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, on that particular day, talk by telephone with Safet Hadzialijagic, the president of the local community of the Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that specific detail, but I did have some telephone conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll go on to that. On that particular day, did you talk to Mr. Sulejman Tihic, who was the president of the SDA of the municipal board of Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, I absolutely did not talk to Mr. Sulejman, nor did I see him at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Can you confirm that you talked over the telephone with Mr. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I was present when Mr. Pero Vasiljevic talked to him, and he received a telephone number from him, and later on we were to talk to some other people using that number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a telephone conversation with Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SALKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
