utterances.text: As I said previously, Your Honour, depending of the communication with the witness, about the -- whether he will follow the pattern of the cross-examination, not to go into additional explaining, so on and so forth, well, I would say at least two hours, maybe two and a half. But as you know, I mean, it's very, very rough, rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is for you alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a very rough estimation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Also we were informed that Mr. Dagovic will come this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Let's just deal with Mr. Tihic because he's waiting to be called. So you think you'll take two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Something like that. Maybe three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, about how long do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Forty minutes to one hour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Forty minutes to one hour? That's too wide. I'll make it one hour, for cross-examination, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will try to my best to limit myself to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Forty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our estimation is something like two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: A fast estimate would be a total of seven hours, I think. MR. DI FAZIO: That takes us to about Thursday morning, I think, by my rough calculations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just to be on the safer side, because I usually don't like really stopping counsel in cross-examination, for obvious reasons, because sometimes the answers bring some more questions. MR. DI FAZIO: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Sometimes. And it's better that we complete what they need to complete. MR. DI FAZIO: Thursday morning on those estimations. Even if things don't go well, don't go smoothly, say, even to the end of Thursday. We've still got Friday to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because we need to include the time for re-examination, and usually re-examination will depend on the issues raised on cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: I was a bit longer than I expected to be today, but I would hope to keep it short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may address the second issue about the sitting hours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think, with all due respect, that this is possible, because I have been conferring with my client about his well-being and his medical status at this moment, and he says, as I previously told this Trial Chamber, that he is -- by sitting until 5.00, it is about the limit he can really bear at this moment. This, today, he also experienced another problem that the new nurse came, which is inexperienced, so -- I mean, Your Honours, there is so many problems, we have to deal with that - I mean just logistics - that I don't really -- I really don't think that it is achievable, with the -- we are trying on our side, as Defence, to limit, as you have seen, about the Mr. Tihic's cross-examination, we tried to really expedite this trial. We are doing our best. But this is something we cannot really compromise on that. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure that everybody is trying to do their best. And the authorities in the Tribunal are also concerned about the welfare of Mr. Milan Simic; that is why they are trying to provide whatever they can provide. And we also have a duty to get the trial going. So if we all stick to the hours mentioned for cross-examination and perhaps re-examination, perhaps we can cut off sitting beyond 1700 hours, especially due to Mr. Milan Simic's condition, so that it wouldn't be in anybody's interests if his health broke down before we finish the witnesses who are directly mentioning him in the charges against him. So we will revise our sitting schedules and stick to completing our proceedings each day at 1700 hours; that is, today -- no. Today it is because of the special Plenary. Tomorrow, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. So we'll change the hours only up to 1700 hours; the usual lunch break, 1300 hours to 1530. I hope that will be of some help to Mr. Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, my client just informed me -- he called me over there, and I had to excuse myself to go over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He says that he is experiencing very strong difficulties today, and with the Court's permission, he would like to rest tomorrow in UNDU.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: At the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the Detention Unit, and not come into the Court, because he doesn't feel well. That is his -- but as I understood him, we can go on with the trial tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because it's the cross-examination, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes, that will be granted. He can be excused. He can rest the whole day tomorrow, because we are just dealing with cross-examination of a witness he has already heard himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You're welcome. So the Registry assistant will inform the relevant officers, please, for tomorrow only. Yes, Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry to burden the Chamber with even more problems --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry to burden the Chamber with even more problems, but better to deal with them now than later, and that's the question of who do we call next. Now, as the Chamber rightly pointed out, estimates are we'll finish Thursday this witness, perhaps late Thursday, but that still leaves Friday. Now, I propose to call - Mr. Weiner will take that witness - I propose to call Ewa Tabeau. But, as I said, the Prosecution doesn't want to do that if it's going to result in split testimony, in other words, her examination-in-chief on one occasion and then, at a later stage, after other witnesses, she's called back for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, because, you see, we cannot limit the cross-examination. If she is going to start on Friday, for instance, and then - I don't know how long you will take. Maybe one hour or so - and then we have four Defence counsels to cross-examine. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I think -- I'm sorry. Perhaps I didn't make myself clear. I've got no problem with her going off during that break in the following week and then finishing off her cross-examination, but what I understood from Defence counsel was this: They're happy for her to give her evidence in chief and then for her to be adjourned off at a later date, much later date, in the same way --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. Next week, after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because next week we are not sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After the break. MR. DI FAZIO: I see. Perhaps I've misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Let me confirm with the Defence counsels. My understanding is that this expert witness will come and give evidence possibly on Friday, maybe the examination-in-chief will be completed, but that the Defence counsels are saying they would need more time to prepare for cross-examination, in which case they wouldn't be ready to start cross-examination right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They would rather have the cross-examination after our break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. A hundred per cent, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In addition, allow me to say, Madam President, that in light of the fact that Mr. Milan Simic tomorrow will not come here, we propose to have a shorter lunch break, so we can start at 2.30 p.m., and to have sitting hours until 5.00, if it fits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- if it's fine with all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that is a possibility, because we won't need the long lunch break, and we can revise the sitting hours. Perhaps start at 14.30, have a break at 1600 hours, and continue at 1630 to -- from 1630 - how much is one and a half hours? - have another one and a half hours. I'm very bad at maths.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 1830, Your Honour. It's 1830, if we have a 30-minute --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, have two sessions in the afternoon as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Two sessions in the morning, two sessions in the afternoon. Yes, that's perfectly okay. The Prosecution? Because that will complete cross-examination much faster. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got no problem with that at all. I'm happy to sit those hours. And I think it's a fine suggestion. And if the Chamber is happy with that, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For tomorrow only, because Mr. Milan Simic will be resting. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. That's fine. I've got no problem with that. And if the Chamber wants that, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll confirm that with the Registry assistant after finding out from the other trials whether they will not use the Trial Chamber. So that is a proposal which the Trial Chamber is pleased to accept, subject to the Registry being prepared to prepare the courtroom for that. And then on Thursday and Friday, if Mr. Simic is able to come on Thursday, then we go back to our normal hours, up to 1700 hours only. All right? MR. DI FAZIO: The problem -- I have no problem with that either. And what I'm foreshadowing is what happens when we've finished with Mr. Simic. That's what I'm concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When we are finished with Mr. Tihic. MR. DI FAZIO: With Mr. Tihic, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. But I thought we were agreed that the examination-in-chief of the expert witness can go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, okay. Well, what if that's an hour or two hours? Then we might be left with an afternoon or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. MR. DI FAZIO: Do you see what I mean? And I'm concerned that the Chamber will then say, "Well, where's your next witness," and what do we do in that situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are having too many problems. I think what we can do is -- I can't say, but I thought that the Prosecution -- the Defence counsels would be perhaps ready with maybe another witness where they would go into cross-examination right away. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't know. There is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because right now we don't know whether Mr. Milan Simic will be well enough to come on Thursday, after resting tomorrow, so we can't even say whether or not we can bring another witness directly concerning Mr. Milan Simic. So let's leave it at that. Let's see what happens. Can we start Mr. Tihic, please? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, very well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And who is going to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tihic. You are still under solemn declaration. We are now going to start cross-examination, and thereafter the Prosecution will do their re-examination. So Mr. Zecevic is starting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Zecevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Tihic. I'm going to ask you a few questions with respect to your testimony about a month ago. You recall your testimony, do you not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tihic, if I understood you correctly, you were a judge, prosecutor, and then an attorney. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is perhaps a good moment, Mr. Tihic, for you to clarify one point. As an experienced lawyer, I'm sure you can tell us something about some relevant legal provisions in the BH republic in 1992.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Tihic, if you know, and I assume you do: The possession of automatic weapons, such as a Kalashnikov or some similar weapon, was not possible legally, was it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Possessing such a weapon was a criminal act in conformity with the Criminal Code of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was a criminal act or an offence - I can't quite remember - or a misdemeanour. But anyway, something along those lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was punishment if somebody had committed this offence, misdemeanour, or crime?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and probably a fine would have been incurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A fine for the possession of illegal automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been a fine, yes, depending on the case, and if it was a recidivist or if it was a first-time offender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but there was a prison sentence as well?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably as an alternative. Both were possible: fines and terms in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean, Mr. Tihic, that the deprivation of freedom for people who are suspected of having committed the crime or misdemeanour would be in keeping with the legal provisions?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it wasn't a crime for which the sentence of deprivation of freedom is prescribed. It is not so grievous as to merit that sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about arrest.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that a person would be arrested for having committed that particular act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, I'm asking you whether the competent authorities in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina - and I mean the police force first and foremost - did they have the authority to undertake measures? If somebody was suspected of being in possession of arms illegally, could they arrest that person and could they file a criminal report and undertake proceedings against them?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been cause for detention and interrogation, but not for a prison sentence; otherwise you would have to incarcerate half of Bosnia. But formally and legally, it was not such a serious crime which would imply a prison sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not -- I was just asking you about an arrest, whether an arrest would be warranted. Thank you. Mr. Tihic, another matter: You were incarcerated, if I remember your testimony rightly, at the SUP building and the TO building in the first few days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A total of about 50 people were incarcerated there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said, Mr. Tihic, that most of them were Muslims and Croats as regards ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the overall population, approximately speaking, if you can tell me, of the Croats and Muslims as an ethnic group, an ethnic community in Samac, in the town of Samac, taken together, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the town itself, in the town proper, there were 40 per cent to 45 per cent Muslims; 15 per cent were Croats; 20 per cent was the maximum for the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that mean about 3.000 people were Muslims and Croats, taken together? Would I be correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say three and a half thousand, a little more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, Mr. Tihic: After the elections in 1990, you were elected deputy of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, if you recall: The budget of Bosanski Samac for 1990 [as interpreted] was never adopted, was it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tihic, you are the vice-president of the Assembly of Republika Srpska at the moment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your professional career is linked to legislation, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Political. The rest was tied up with --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I was -- I was told that there is a problem with the transcript. It's page 9625. It says "1990," and the question was "1992." Would you like me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The budget for 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can repeat the question, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Tihic. There was an error in the transcript. Could you repeat? I asked you with regard to the budget for 1992.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the budget for 1992 was adopted or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Tihic: Looking at your C.V., you have had a lot of practical experience, because you worked in the judiciary.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also have experience in the legislative branch of government at the level both of the municipality and the republic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Tihic, you must be aware of the fact that the Republic of Srpska had very lively legislative activity in 1992.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in that year, the constitution and a lot of legislation, a large number of decrees, decisions, were adopted?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that was enacted was annulled by the constitutional court of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I know some things were adopted, but the constitutional court annulled it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to the decisions and the decrees enacted by Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decrees adopted in 1992 up to the beginning of the aggression were rendered null and void. I know that the constitutional court of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina rendered some of these null and void, and none of this was published in the Official Gazette, so I could not have been aware of it. We considered these institutions to be parastate institutions. They were not legal. They were not part of the system, so what they issued was not valid, up to the signing of the Dayton Accord when Republika Srpska was recognised. That was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like the usher to help me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now show you some documents, Mr. Tihic, and I would like you to identify them and see whether we agree on their contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the extract of Official Gazette of Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina dated Monday, 8 June 1992, number 10, and the actual document is an executive order of some kind. It has a number 176 as a decision. You can put the English version on the ELMO. MR. DI FAZIO: Is there an English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is. Oh, I'm sorry, we didn't have the time to -- we gave it to the translation department, but we never got the -- of all these documents, we don't have translation, Your Honours. So what I will do is ask the witness to read the name of the executive decision, and then we will mark it for the identification, and after we have the translation, then we will ask that it be admitted to evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, provided that all the questions, whatever questions you have, will be based on the passages that the witness will be asked to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours, but I'm not going to go into the contents of the executive orders or any other documents which I am about to present. I just want the witness to explain the nature of these documents -- of these executive orders, nothing else. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I don't want to be seen to be agreeing to the admissibility of this document at this stage. I'm happy for it to be marked for identification. I'd just like to ascertain whether it was ever disclosed to us and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because before the English translation, really you can't be in a position to state your position. MR. DI FAZIO: Exactly, so I remain at liberty to object at a later stage if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, these documents have been disclosed to the Prosecutor by myself. Let me remind the Prosecutor those are the Official Gazettes number 8, 10 and 12 of 1992, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But they were still in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were disclosed to the Prosecutor in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we will go by the system I have elaborated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could we have the number for identification purposes, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D11/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be kind enough to read what it says in the letterhead, I mean the title above Monday, the 8th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 8, page 311."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the decree?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decree on organising and performing work obligation for the needs of defence."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] Your Honour, could we have the second document? Maybe the Registrar can just give it subnumbers under the -- no? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: She will decide how to number them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D12/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please bear with me, Your Honours, just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, would you be so kind as to do --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Monday, 8th of June, 1992, Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 8, page 317."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read the decision 189?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decision on the functioning and protection of businesses and industrial plants under conditions of an imminent threat of war in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tihic. [In English] Could the usher help me with the third document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D13/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, I apologise for troubling you like this, but because we do not have versions in English, it is necessary for you to read this.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Page 318, number 8, Official Gazette," and it's probably of the Serbian people, but it's not legible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 189?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Order on restarting production and on stocks of finished products."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could we have the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D14/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Page 356, number 10, Official Gazette of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Tuesday, the 30th of June, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read decree number 275? It's the first one on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decree on the manner of safe removal of animal carcasses and other inedible animal parts and products under conditions of threat of war."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, again.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Tuesday, the 30th of June, 1992, Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 10, page 361."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, if you can, read decision 279.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D15/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could please read decision 279, Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decision on the manner of determining remuneration, compensation for work in state organs and companies."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] May we have the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D16/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Tuesday, the 30th of June, 1992, Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 10, page 369. Decision on limiting the prices of staple foodstuffs on the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tihic. [In English] Could we have the next one, please. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D17/2 ter ID. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there is a matter that I'm grateful to Mr. Weiner for having pointed it out to me, and it relates to this. I think I should raise it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: That's this Rule 90(H)(i), says that cross-examination has got to be limited to the subject matter of the evidence-in-chief and matters affecting the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And? MR. DI FAZIO: And where the witness is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party to the subject matter of the case. To the subject matter of the case. Now, I don't -- obviously it's not -- this documentation and this issue can't go to the issue of credibility, and I don't see how it arose -- how it arises from anything that occurred in the context of anything that was said in the evidence-in-chief of this witness. And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But what about any matter that may support the Defence case of the cross-examining party? MR. DI FAZIO: It doesn't say that. That Rule doesn't say that. Now, I suggest that -- what I'm concerned about is that Mr. Zecevic might be using this witness essentially just to present his case, and that's what concerns me, and the operation of the Rule may well prevent that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This was (H)(i)? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. These are documents produced by the Republika Srpska in a period of time when this witness was incarcerated. Now, it's got somehow to be relevant to the case for the cross-examining party. Now, I don't know if it is or isn't relevant. I can't see what the relevance of it is at this stage. If Mr. Zecevic can explain how it becomes relevant or -- then I withdraw my objection, but at this stage, try as I will, I can't see what the relevance of this material is to his case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which material? The documents? MR. DI FAZIO: These decisions, this material that's going in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why don't we wait for his questions, and see? MR. DI FAZIO: As Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because he's just asking the witness to identify what these are. And a part of the problem in this case is who was in power, who was who, state-wise. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps what I'll do is hope Mr. Zecevic bears in mind what I've said, and I'll sit down, and perhaps he can continue, but at some point, that will have to be demonstrated, the relevance of this material will have to be demonstrated. Otherwise, I'd like it to be known that I will be objecting to its admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, and I think the other thing that must be borne in mind in this trial, where we have four people, is that sometimes Defence counsel share which areas of the case they will cross-examine. It may not necessarily be only cross-examining only on the charges facing the accused. And that sharing of topics does save time, because otherwise each counsel would have to repeat what they think is for their case. MR. DI FAZIO: I appreciate that, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Zecevic has understood what you're saying. MR. DI FAZIO: It's something that, as I watch this material come in, it concerns me, and I just raise it for Mr. Zecevic's consideration and so that he knows the position of the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, and I will not allow Mr. Zecevic to explain in reply. Just go ahead with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very shortly, Your Honour, we believe we are entitled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. It's simply a matter of time because the Chamber has no problem at all. Just go ahead with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Page 372, number 10, Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Tuesday, the 30th of June, 1992."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, would you read us the instruction numbered 300?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Instruction on increased security of -- for supplying households with potable water."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are we going with the numbers in sequence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we shall always wait for the Registry assistant to give us the number. I think it's much better that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was trying to save time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we would rather have a clearer record, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D18/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page -- I think it's page 400. It's a little bit illegible, but the Official Gazette is number 12, "Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Friday, the 31st of July, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read decree 358.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decree on the temporary use of flats, business premises and residential buildings."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D19/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Page 430, number 12, Official Gazette of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Friday, the 31st of July, 1992. Decree on the work recruitment of the population in gathering the harvest."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. Tell me, Mr. Tihic, could you explain briefly what a decree is to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A decree is a by-law issued by the government on the basis of its authority and the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And a decision? Is that also a by-law?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A decision is also a statutory act, but it can be issued by other bodies, other than the government. It can also be an assembly or a ministry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tihic, as far as you know, I assume you are seeing these documents for the first time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm seeing them for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt that this is legislation passed by the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Tihic, at the beginning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let's just be clear, I'm sorry, Mr. Zecevic on the question you asked Mr. Tihic, when you say -- he has answered that he has no doubt that this is legislation passed by Republika Srpska. Is it still in -- this legislation is still in force or was it the legislation --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was the legislation to the relevant time of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's no longer in force?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, you're asking me a million dollar question, really, because some of it is probably during the time it has been changed, some of it is in force, and some of it is not in force any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So we limit it to the relevant time covered by the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's limited to the relevant time in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, you said a minute ago, in answer to my question about decrees and decisions, that they were not published in Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These Official Gazettes have a basic flaw. They are said to be official gazettes of the people. People do not have official gazettes; municipalities do, and other bodies. No nation, no people issues a gazette; it's a state that issues a gazette. These gazettes were not available at the time. They may have been printed somewhere, but I was not able, as an ordinary man, to get hold of them. Maybe the government did issue these things somewhere, but it's very strange that they say it's an official gazette of the people. It is states, entities, cantons that publish official gazettes, not the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please bear with me, Your Honours. Can I have a minute, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned the decision of the constitutional court of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Tihic, did you mean the decision of October 1992, by which the declaration of the Serbian people on the establishing of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was rendered null and void? Is that the decision you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must mean 1991, not 1992.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly what the title of this document was, whether it was a declaration or whether it was a constitution. But the constitutional court rendered null and void the document concerning the establishment of Republika Srpska, and if that was rendered null and void, then all the other by-laws stemming from it were not valid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you fully.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's from my point of view, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just clarify something. Are you referring to the decision by which the fundamental piece of legislation was rendered null and void, thereby rendering null and void all the other documents stemming from it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This means that none of these lower-level documents were directly annulled by the constitutional court.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not one by one, not individually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tihic. We shall agree that these regulations that you glanced through in fact represent matters falling within the competence of the executive branch of government; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "the executive branch of government," you also mean the executive committee of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but these were not issued by the executive committee of the municipality, what we just read. But in a broader sense, yes, yes, an executive committee is part of the executive branch of government at a lower level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it up to the executive branch to enforce this legislation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Tihic, to move on to another topic: At the time of these events in April 1992, you were the president of the town committee of the SDA, the town board in Bosanski Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you wrote a book of memoirs?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I was released from camp in 1992, I made notes in the order that these events came back to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this book -- shall we say it's a book?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, in this book you described in detail all the events you could recall pertaining to the time before and after the 17th of April, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. Not in total detail, but yes, quite extensively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask the usher to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could I have the document D3/2 ter ID, D3/2 ter ID. Could you put the English version on the ELMO and the original one before Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to look at it? Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this document. I see what it's about, but I don't remember that this document was issued to Hasan Bicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name typed here where the signature is?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it wasn't I who signed it, and I don't remember that there was any need to issue this certificate to Hasan Bicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Hasan Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know him well?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was an innkeeper in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, but if he was, it was only on paper. He wasn't active, not active enough to warrant this sort of certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his brother, Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know him?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the SDA also?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. If he was, he wasn't one of the active people. They were more concerned with their own private business enterprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot remember having issued this document to Hasan Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I probably didn't. It's more likely that I didn't, because I see no reason for issuing Hasan with this certificate. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea what sort of materiel and technical equipment could have been referred to on the 13th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's precisely because of this. I don't think Hasan could have got hold of this sort of certificate. Materiel and technical equipment could refer to anything. But at that time, this was just before the attack on Samac. This could not have been issued to Hasan, no way. I remember on one occasion issuing a similar certificate, but this referred to other persons - and I think I mentioned it in my testimony - but not for Hasan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say you issued such certificates.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued just one other one, and that was for Fuad Jasenica and Ibrahim Salkic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, it's 1700 hours. We'll adjourn --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tihic. We'll continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and we will resume our proceedings tomorrow at 0930 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
